en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and is critically endangered due to severe deforestation.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government is composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives, which make the laws.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago by carving steps into the mountains of the Cordilleras.
The Barong Tagalog is the national costume of the Philippines, traditionally made of delicate pineapple fiber called piña.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for babies.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a vibrant two-step forward, one-step backward dance ritual.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where characters represent syllables, and it was traditionally carved on bamboo and leaves.
Intramuros is the historic walled city in Manila that served as the seat of the Spanish colonial government for over 300 years.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Oblation statue at the University of the Philippines.
Apolinario Mabini, known as the Brains of the Revolution, drafted the decrees for the First Philippine Republic despite his paralysis.
